subject: Animation
title: The Flintstones: Prime-Time Animation Begins
description: A fast breakdown of The Flintstones: Prime-Time Animation Begins for builders.

hook.text: In 1960, The Flintstones became the first animated series to air in prime time on American television.

buildup.text: Hanna-Barbera created the show as an animated version of The Honeymooners set in the Stone Age.

discovery.text: The show aired on ABC at 8:30 PM Friday nights, directly competing with live-action sitcoms.

twist.text: Despite being a cartoon, it was originally aimed at adults. Cigarette companies were early sponsors.

climax.text: The Flintstones proved animation could hold a prime-time audience and paved the way for The Simpsons.

punchline.text: A Stone Age family launched the era of prime-time cartoons.

quiz.question: What was groundbreaking about The Flintstones when it debuted in 1960?
options: It was the first color cartoon
It was the first animated series to air in prime time, competing with live-action shows
It was the first cartoon to use computers

details.summary: The Flintstones premiered in 1960 as the first animated series in prime-time television. It proved animation could attract adult audiences, not just children, laying the groundwork for every adult animated show that followed.
details.whyItMatters: Without The Flintstones proving animation's prime-time viability, The Simpsons, South Park, and the entire adult animation genre might never have existed. It opened a door that transformed television.
takeaways: The Flintstones was TV's first prime-time animated series in 1960
It proved animation could attract adult audiences and sponsors
It established the sitcom formula that adult animation still uses

faq.question: How did The Flintstones change television?
faq.answer: It proved animated shows could air in prime time and attract adult viewers and major sponsors. Before The Flintstones, animation was considered exclusively children's entertainment. It opened the door for decades of adult animated shows.

faq.question: Why did The Flintstones work for adult audiences?
faq.answer: It borrowed heavily from The Honeymooners, a popular live-action sitcom. The prehistoric setting added visual humor while the domestic comedy resonated with adult viewers. It was essentially a sitcom that happened to be drawn.
